title: Flowise public chatflow responses disclose MCP bearer tokens
summary: The public-chatflows endpoint exposes MCP server bearer tokens. A caller can reuse a leaked token to invoke the chatflow despite its API-key protection and consume model quota.

severity.rationale: An unauthenticated response can disclose a usable bearer credential. The issue is especially relevant to model-backed automation exposed through MCP.

affected.note: CVE range: 3.1.3 through 3.1.4. No fixed version is established in the inspected record.

exposure: A reachable affected public chatflow with MCP server configuration is required. The vendor has ended core operations and archived the project.

params.instructions: Check Flowise version, affected release line and the documented exposure conditions.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Remove untrusted access to affected public chatflows and replace the unsupported deployment with a maintained implementation or reviewed fix. No vendor fixed version is established here.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm unauthenticated access to public chatflows with MCP server configuration has been removed.
Confirm any exposed MCP bearer tokens have been rotated and the old tokens no longer authorize chatflow invocation.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
Replaced the unsupported fixed-version verification with access-removal and credential-rotation checks.
